bodies.intuition: When the input and the output are different things — a French sentence and its English translation — one stack can read the input with no restrictions while another writes the output one token at a time. The reader sees everything at once; the writer sees only what it has already produced, plus whatever it pulls from the reader.
bodies.engineer: An unmasked encoder stack and a causally masked decoder stack, joined by cross-attention where the decoder's queries meet the encoder's keys and values. It costs roughly twice the parameters of a decoder alone, and it remains the better fit where the input is genuinely a fixed object to be consumed rather than a prefix to be continued.
bodies.math: Encoder produces H = Enc(x) once. Each decoder layer runs masked self-attention over y_{<t}, then cross-attention with Q from the decoder and K, V from H. H is computed once and reused at every decoding step.

emphasis.intuition: The reader sees everything at once
